comments.body: Root cause confirmed on origin/main 1c8a67702f8. The handler that outlives the test is the entrypoint stderr handler (marker _rebar_stderr_handler) built by install_stderr_handler in src/rebar/_logging.py as StreamHandler(sys.stderr), installed by rebar._cli.main (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:316-318). A scratch pytest plugin listing the rebar logger's handlers after each test showed that, after test_cli_passed_but_unsigned_is_exit_11_with_byte_identical_stderr, this handler holds that test's capsys CaptureIO with closed=True and stays attached for the next test. The install is idempotent by marker, so later main() calls never rebind it. Production is at fault: any in-process caller whose sys.stderr is swapped or closed gets dead or misdirected diagnostics. Polluter: the first test on a worker to call rebar._cli.main under capsys; in the reported pair, the plan-review CLI test. A second, test-side order dependence: the plan-review test's byte-identical stderr assertion also captured _seed's output, which logs an unsigned-write warning once any earlier main() has installed the handler; with a lazy-stderr probe it failed in order verify,plan-review. Fix: _CurrentStderrHandler resolves sys.stderr at emit time (the pattern of the stdlib's logging._StderrHandler), and the plan-review test drains seeding output before main(). Evidence: tests/unit/test_logging_stderr_target.py fails 2 of 2 on the old _logging.py (ValueError: I/O operation on closed file) and passes 2 of 2 after. The pair passes in both orders, and both facade modules together pass 29 of 29 in both orders (-p no:randomly -p no:xdist). tests/interfaces plus the logging/CLI/MCP/reconciler modules: 2841 passed, 12 skipped. make lint and make typecheck exit 0.

Cause, confirmed locally (fails on that commit, passes with origin/main _logging.py): compact.py:389 wraps the fold in contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()), and the timing line logs inside it, so a handler that follows sys.stderr writes into the discarded buffer. Revised approach (description updated): the handler writes to sys.__stderr__, the process stream, which neither pytest capture nor redirect_stderr swaps. New regression tests: 3 fail on origin/main's _logging.py and 3 fail on the first-attempt handler; all 3 pass on the revision. test_compact_fold_prelock.py passes 10/10; the facade pair passes in both orders; both facade modules pass 29/29 in both orders.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## Hypothesis confirmed, with a deterministic reproduction

Posting from a parallel session that hit these same failures in an unrelated `make verify`
(3 failed, 20648 passed, 2:18:13). This ticket is claimed elsewhere, so this is evidence
only — no code changed here.

**The repro does not need the full suite or xdist.** Two tests, in this order, in one
process, on a clean `origin/main` tree at `7c3cb5e9a4f`:

```
pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_plan_review_attestation_facades.py::test_cli_passed_but_unsigned_is_exit_11_with_byte_identical_stderr \
       tests/interfaces/facades/test_verify_completion_facades.py::test_cli_llm_error_is_clean_exit_one \
       -p no:randomly -p no:cacheprovider
```

→ `1 failed, 1 passed`. Each passes alone (16.36s and 8.92s). Reversing the pair passes.

**The error is exactly the stale-stream write**, captured in full:

```
--- Logging error ---
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../logging/__init__.py", line 1163, in emit
    stream.write(msg + self.terminator)
ValueError: I/O operation on closed file.
Call stack:
  ...
  File "src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py", line 357, in _apply_authorship
    logger.warning(
Message: 'authorship: signing SKIPPED for event %s on %s — %s; writing unsigned'
```

So the mechanism is established, not merely plausible: `_logging.py:81` binds the stream
object at construction, the `_HANDLER_MARKER` early-return (`:74-77`) means no later call
rebinds it, and `logging` reports the write failure to the *current* `sys.stderr`, which the
later test is capturing. That stray report is what trips `"Traceback" not in err`.

Two notes that may save a cycle:

- **Which tests fail is not stable**, because it depends on which test calls `main()` first
  on a given xdist worker. Under `-n 4 --dist worksteal` the set varies run to run, so a
  fix should be validated against the deterministic pair above rather than against a full
  run coming back green once.
- **The production path is affected too, not just tests.** Any embedder that replaces
  `sys.stderr` after the first rebar entrypoint call keeps writing to the original stream.
  A fix that resolves `sys.stderr` at emit time covers both; a pytest fixture that resets
  handlers covers only the tests, and would add an `autouse_fixture` — a ratcheted mechanism
  kind — to work around a library bug.

## A third failure in the same run, probably unrelated

`tests/unit/test_fetch_common_dir_coordination.py::test_uncoordinated_parallel_fetches_can_race_but_coordination_prevents_it`
also failed. It is undiagnosed and shares no obvious cause with this one; flagging it so a
green run here is not read as covering it.

## Duplicates

`4c58-45d4-aaf7-48dc` (fibre-beamy-angora, open) and `7773-cca2-da72-4a0c`
(dicey-acute-finwhale, created by this session before the match surfaced) describe the same
defect. Both are now linked `duplicates` to this ticket; `7773-cca2` is archived.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

On 2026-11-04, `make verify` on macOS failed 2 default-tier tests whose asserted stderr starts with a `--- Logging error ---` traceback (`ValueError: I/O operation on closed file`):

- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_plan_review_attestation_facades.py::test_cli_passed_but_unsigned_is_exit_11_with_byte_identical_stderr`
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_verify_completion_facades.py::test_cli_llm_error_is_clean_exit_one`

This breaks every local `make verify` whenever both land on one xdist worker. The failing record is the `rebar._commands._seam._apply_authorship` warning `authorship: signing SKIPPED ...`, emitted while the test seeds its ticket.

Reproduced on origin/main 1c8a67702f8: running the plan-review test then the verify-completion test in one process (`-p no:randomly -p no:xdist`) fails the second, 3 of 3 runs; the verify test alone passes.

### Root cause (confirmed by probe)

A scratch pytest plugin listed the `rebar` logger's handlers after each test. After the plan-review test, the handler stamped `_rebar_stderr_handler` holds that test's `capsys` `CaptureIO`, now `closed=True`; it is still attached during the next test.

- Production: `install_stderr_handler` (`src/rebar/_logging.py:81`) builds `logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)`, freezing the stderr object current at install time. It is idempotent by marker (`_logging.py:73-75`), so later `rebar._cli.main` calls (`src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:316-318`) never rebind it. Any in-process caller of `main` whose `sys.stderr` is later replaced or closed (pytest capture, `contextlib.redirect_stderr`, an embedding application) gets diagnostics written to a dead or wrong stream. The polluting test in the pair is the plan-review test (the first in-process `main` call under `capsys`); in the full tier, it is whichever CLI test calls `main` first on that worker.
- Test: the plan-review test asserts byte-identical stderr, but its capture also includes `_seed`'s output (line 85, before `main` at line 87). Whether seeding logs anything depends on whether an earlier test already installed the handler. A probe that rebinds the handler to the current `sys.stderr` made the pair pass in order A,B, and made the plan-review test fail in order B,A with the seeding warning as an extra first line.

## Approach

1. Production fix: make the entrypoint handler write to the process's stderr, `sys.__stderr__`, resolved at emit time. Add a `logging.StreamHandler` subclass in `src/rebar/_logging.py` whose `stream` property returns `sys.__stderr__` (falling back to `sys.stderr` when the interpreter has none, e.g. `pythonw`); `install_stderr_handler` installs it in place of `StreamHandler(sys.stderr)`. The marker, idempotency, level resolution, formatter, and stderr-only contract are unchanged. This fits because diagnostics belong to the process stream, not to whichever in-process object is current: pytest capture and embedders swap `sys.stderr` (the stale-stream bug), and rebar itself captures command output with `contextlib.redirect_stderr` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:389`, a `2>/dev/null` emulation), where diagnostics must not be swallowed (`run_sweep` in `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py`: the detached child's stderr is the worker log, pinned by `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py::test_the_detached_sweep_worker_writes_the_timing_line_to_its_log`). Neither swaps `sys.__stderr__`. One handler class fixes all 4 entrypoints (CLI, MCP server, reconciler, compact sweep).
2. Test fix: in the plan-review test, discard captured output after `_seed` (`capsys.readouterr()`), so its byte-identical assertion covers only the CLI command's stderr, which is what its docstring says it pins.

No autouse fixture, no new mechanism, no test reordering, retry, or skip.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_logging.py`: add the lazy-stderr handler class; use it in `install_stderr_handler`.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_plan_review_attestation_facades.py`: drain seeding output before invoking `main`.
- `tests/unit/test_logging_stderr_target.py` (new): regression tests.

## Testing

New `tests/unit/test_logging_stderr_target.py`, isolating the `rebar` logger with `monkeypatch.setattr` on its `handlers` list and level (no autouse fixture):

Each test monkeypatches `sys.__stderr__` to a buffer P standing in for the process stderr.

- Happy path: install the handler while `sys.stderr` is buffer A, close A, replace `sys.stderr` with buffer B, log a warning on a `rebar.*` logger. Assert P holds exactly the formatted line and B has no `--- Logging error ---`. Fails before the fix (record goes to closed A, the logging-error traceback lands in B).
- Failure path: a warning logged inside `contextlib.redirect_stderr(D)` reaches P and leaves D empty (guards the compaction worker log).
- Edge: a second `install_stderr_handler` call after a swap still leaves exactly 1 marked handler, and output reaches P.

Then run `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py`, the 2 facade tests together in both orders, both facade modules together, the CLI facade/contract modules with exact-stderr assertions (`tests/interfaces/facades/`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/`, `tests/interfaces/queries/test_validate_compute.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_repair_pause_ownership_store.py`, `tests/unit/test_logging_level.py`, `tests/unit/reconciler/orchestrate/`), plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`, with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on `PATH` and Jira variables unset. CI's `Verified` vote covers the full default tier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The handler that outlives the test is identified, with the code that installs it: the marked handler from `install_stderr_handler` (`src/rebar/_logging.py`), installed by `rebar._cli.main`; recorded in a ticket comment.
- [x] The 2 tests above pass when run together in one process in either order (`pytest -p no:randomly -p no:xdist <A> <B>` and `<B> <A>`), both exit 0.
- [x] Both facade modules together pass with `-p no:randomly -p no:xdist` (exit 0).
- [x] `tests/unit/test_logging_stderr_target.py` fails on origin/main's `_logging.py` and passes after the fix (both runs recorded in a ticket comment).
- [x] `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py` passes (exit 0), so diagnostics still reach the detached sweep's worker log.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0.
- [x] `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [x] [non-codebase] The change gets `Verified +1` in Gerrit, which runs the full default tier. Evidence: Gerrit change 3309 patch set 2 (revision 9f3a6545d11ae02c6dd19374a17135a013ee9411) received `Verified +1` from rebar CI bot at 2026-11-04 13:43 PST and `LLM-Review +1`; submitted 2026-11-04 13:43 PST as merged commit a9300a8b2f2ea0c93b41aee1b6402f0f7f6fe750.
      provenance: environment=rebar.solutions.navateam.com (Gerrit, project rebar); principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — votes read from the production Gerrit REST API (`/a/changes/3309?o=DETAILED_LABELS`), the same server whose votes gate the merge.
